A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fourier Head work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-density, audio-classification, Decision Transformer, Chronos forecasting, and smoothness-validation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, continuous-density experiments, Llama sampling, additional Atari games, and scaling ablations.

M1.justification: v1 mentions continuous maximum-likelihood training as a possibility; v2 Appendix C.3 implements a continuous variant returning Fourier coefficients and trained on unquantized observations. This extends the training/output procedure while retaining the autocorrelation-based construction in Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: v2 adds BankHeist, DoubleDunk, and Gravitar alongside Seaquest, prompted Llama Gaussian sampling, and an unquantized density-estimation scenario. The synthetic suite replaces the min/max-centered GMM condition with a distinct signed-Beta distribution while retaining Gaussian and GMM-2. Audio and Chronos dataset coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's linear-head comparisons, v2 evaluates a learned two-Gaussian mixture head and pointwise regression in the synthetic experiments, plus GMM-MLE against Fourier-MLE. The sampling experiment also compares the original Llama model and its LoRA-tuned version against the Fourier-head adaptation.

E3.justification: Toy MSE prediction changes from the most likely bin in v1 Section 4 to the distribution's expected value in v2 Section 4.1. New experiments introduce continuous KL/perplexity evaluation, Llama sampling evaluated through 20-bin histograms and sample diversity, and systematic model-size and dataset-size sweeps.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing frequency, regularization, and binning studies, v2 tests whether advantages persist across model and dataset sizes for Decision Transformer and Chronos (Figures 14–15 and 18–19). It also adds continuous-MLE frequency analyses, regression case studies, and sampling-diversity analyses (Figures 9–12).

E5.justification: v2 reports ten seeds for the new sampling study and four-seed dataset-size averages and three-seed model-size averages for new Chronos ablations. Existing four-seed toy/RL reporting and the 1,000-trial smoothness analysis remain. These disclosures do not establish increased repetitions of retained experiments.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the added comparisons and experiments. For example, v2 Table 5 gives Gaussian KL of 0.026 for GMM versus 0.116 for Fourier, but Beta KL of 0.407 versus 0.191. GMM-2 MSE changes from 0.224/0.211 to 0.126/0.123 for linear/Fourier under the revised prediction rule, so this is not a same-setting gain. Original Seaquest headline returns and Chronos scores are retained.

T1.justification: The smoothness definition, Theorem 3.3, its assumptions, and Appendix A proofs are retained. Limited mathematical changes include correcting the regularizer's coefficient index from c_n to c_k and introducing Appendix C.4's sampling-distance definition, which labels half an L-infinity distance as total variation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the 46% Seaquest headline with improvements across four Atari games of 'as much as 377%'. The central method, scaling-law contribution, and 3.5% Chronos claim remain. The strengthened percentage claim conflicts with Table 2: 1.32 to 4.98 corresponds to approximately 277% improvement.

C2.justification: v2 adds an important distribution-dependent qualification: GMM heads outperform Fourier on Gaussian-family targets, whereas Fourier performs better on Beta. It explains similar MSE across regression and classification heads through prediction of conditional means, and hypothesizes memorization in the LoRA sampling baseline. The introduction also shifts its smoothing explanation from explicit regularization to finite-frequency truncation.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents Decision Transformer training for five epochs, approximately 2.012M parameters, and four hours on one GPU; Chronos training is specified as 200k steps, approximately 20M parameters, and 48 hours on eight GPUs. Appendix C.4 adds prompt construction and LoRA hyperparameters. A reproducibility statement supplies a direct repository link beyond v1's project-page link. These are disclosures, not evidence of changed retained training budgets.

R1.justification: v2 expands sampling-related positioning through Gu, Paruchuri, and discussion of Hopkins, and adds forecasting and classification-related citations. It makes the dependence on De la Fuente's Fourier Basis Density Model more explicit in the introduction and method; that relationship was already acknowledged in v1.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. v2 moves the audio example to Appendix C.1, subdivides the experimental appendices, edits regularization/binning and RL explanations, and adds a reproducibility section and appendix contents list. Much of the introduction, theory, and conclusion is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR typography, margins, and headers and substantially reorganizes displays. The toy plot adds a GMM column and Beta examples, Atari Table 2 becomes a four-game comparison, and the full Chronos table moves to Appendix Table 8 alongside a shorter main-text summary. Numerous sampling, MLE, and scaling figures are added; existing audio and action-distribution figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The GMM/regression controls and non-Gaussian tests substantially strengthen v1's largely linear-head comparisons and clarify when Fourier is advantageous. Additional Atari environments and model/data-size analyses test generality, while training disclosures improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, although the overstated 377% headline and ambiguous L-infinity 'TVD' definition limit confidence in those particular claims.
